jordan_customer: Hey team — our rerank calls started returning VERY strange score ranges this morning (some extremely negative numbers, some >1e6). Also intermittently seeing 400s. Customer reported spike after a billing invoice failed. Any known outages?

alex_cs: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact request body and headers (redact API key)? Also which model and endpoint URL are you calling?

jordan_customer: Pasting sanitized payload:```json
{
  "queries": ["find best answer"],
  "candidates": [["A","B"]],
  "top_k": 5
}
```Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, Content-Type: application/json, X-Org: acme-inc. Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank. Model: rerank-small-v2.

maria_eng: Two quick things to confirm: 1) reranker returns raw logits (not probabilities) by default — large magnitude values can happen depending on the head. We normally recommend normalizing with softmax client-side if you want 0..1 probabilities. 2) Are you batching multiple queries in one request? malformed batching can cause array flattening and weird score alignment.

jordan_customer: We send as single query per request. Example of a 400: ```{
  "error": "invalid request: unexpected token at position 0"
}``` But sometimes we get 200 with scores like -127.5 or 999999.0.

liam_ml: Raw logits that large or negative aren't impossible but 999999 is suspicious (likely a sentinel or parse overflow). Couple hypothese: JSON number truncation, proxy injecting something, or SDK sending strings for numbers. Can you show the exact bytes (curl -v) or a server log line?

jordan_customer: Here's curl verbose (redacted):

```
> POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Content-Type: application/json
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> 
> {"queries":["find best answer"],"candidates":[["A","B"]],"top_k":"5"}
```

alex_cs: Aha. top_k is a string there ("5") — our server will coerce in some paths but older codepaths had a coercion bug that, combined with chunked transfer edge cases, could lead to mis-parsed buffers. That could explain the 400s plus weird scores if parsing hit a fallback.

sam_sre: Also note: Transfer-Encoding: chunked + certain proxies (nginx with chunked on + body rewriting) can sometimes merge chunks incorrectly leading to JSON corruption. We saw similar with another customer where header rewrites changed Content-Type to text/plain which made our JSON parser attempt different number parsing.

jordan_customer: We do route through an internal billing proxy that injects an X-Invoice header and returns 402 when invoice expired. Could that be related?

billing-bot: Invoice status: unpaid (last successful charge failed at 2026-02-12T09:03Z). Policy: proxy will return 402 and a minimal HTML page when unpaid.

maria_eng: If the proxy returned a 402 HTML body but the client still forwarded it (or the proxy streamed an HTML error page into our rerank endpoint because of misrouting), the server could parse that as text and produce malformed numeric fields. Not common but plausible.

liam_ml: For the score semantics: raw reranker logits are unbounded and model-dependent. Typical guidance: apply softmax across candidates to get normalized probabilities; for pairwise rerankers the sign matters but magnitude is relative. We should add clearer docs: "scores are raw logits; to interpret as probabilities use softmax".

alex_cs: For immediate repro steps @jordan_customer: 1) Can you try a direct curl to https://api.redwood.ai:443 (bypass proxy) with Content-Type: application/json and top_k as an integer (no quotes) and Transfer-Encoding disabled (send Content-Length)? 2) If you can reproduce, paste the full raw response body when you see the weird numbers.

jordan_customer: I tested bypassing proxy — direct call returns normal scores (~0.12, -0.03). Going through proxy reproduces 999999 and occasional 400s.

sam_sre: That's a smoking gun. Looks like the billing proxy is sometimes injecting/rewriting content. We'll need proxy logs. Can you open a support ticket with your proxy team and cc us? We'll also temporarily add request validation on our side to reject non-JSON content with 4xx and a clear error message.

liam_ml: Quick mitigation: client-side softmax snippet (JS):```js
function softmax(scores){
  const mx = Math.max(...scores);
  const ex = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s - mx));
  const sum = ex.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
  return ex.map(v => v/sum);
}
```Use that to avoid relying on raw scale.

alex_cs: Internal action items: @maria_eng escalate to docs to add explicit section on "rerank outputs are raw logits" and recommended softmax example; @sam_sre to investigate billing proxy behavior and add defensive validation; @liam_ml to add a short note in SDK to coerce numeric fields and validate types before sending.

maria_eng: I'll draft a docs patch and add a small FAQ entry about 400s caused by non-JSON bodies due to proxies.

sam_sre: We'll also add a deploy that returns 422 with clearer error when Content-Type != application/json or when chunked+top_k non-int detected. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rerank-validate-headers v1.2.3 by sam_sre (canary)->prod

alex_cs: Jordan — can you confirm whether doing direct calls cleared the issue so we can close the support loop with your billing/proxy team?

jordan_customer: Direct calls are clean. I'll loop in proxy/billing team and try again after they fix. Thanks everyone :) :thumbsup:

liam_ml: Follow-up note for internal tracker: observed sentinel-like 999999 originated from an old upstream library that used 999999 as "parse error" float when JSON parse failed for numeric fields. We'll add server-side sanitization to cap extreme scores and return an explicit parse error.

alex_cs: Closing for now but keep us posted. If you hit any 402 HTML bodies forwarded into our API, please paste a raw example and we'll fast-track a fix.
